notes.meaning: A godly parent or teacher urges the young to hold tightly to God's instructions in their hearts, not just memorizing words. Obeying these godly commands brings a long, fruitful life and true inner peace. While this is the general rule for living wisely in God's world, it also points forward to the eternal life God gives His people.

God's people are told to keep faithful love and truth close at all times, wearing them like a necklace and engraving them deep within their thoughts. Living with genuine honesty and love earns respect and good will from both God and neighbors. It reflects God's own character and shows that someone's faith is real.

True wisdom begins by placing complete confidence in the Lord instead of relying on limited human thinking. In every daily decision and life path, believers are called to consult God and follow His will. When we depend on Him, the Lord guides our steps and clears away the obstacles in our journey.

People are warned against pride and thinking they are smart enough to manage without God. Instead, having a healthy reverence for God and turning away from sin brings health to the physical body and refreshes the spirit. Living right with God calms the mind and protects a person from the harmful effects of evil habits.

Believers are called to honor the Lord by giving Him the first and best portion of their income and harvest, rather than keeping it all for themselves. This act shows grateful trust that God provides everything we have. God promises to bless generous givers with plenty, assuring them that they will not suffer loss by putting Him first.

When trials or difficulties come, God's children should not despise them or become bitter. God uses hardships to correct and train us, just as a loving human father disciplines a son he delights in. Experiencing God's discipline is actually proof of His deep love and fatherly care for us.

Finding God's wisdom brings deep happiness that no earthly treasure can match. Wisdom gives greater benefits than silver, pure gold, or sparkling jewels because it gives skill for living and leads to a relationship with God. Nothing a person could ever wish for compares to the value of knowing God's truth.

Wisdom is described like a generous queen offering long life in one hand and honor and provision in the other. Her paths bring true peace of mind and satisfaction rather than sorrow. Like the tree of life in the garden of Eden, wisdom nourishes those who hold fast to it and restores what was lost to sin.

God used His own perfect wisdom and understanding when He laid the earth's foundations and spread out the heavens. By that same knowledge, He caused deep underground waters to flow and clouds to give gentle dew. Because wisdom built the world, anyone who walks in wisdom lives in harmony with how creation was designed to work.

A student of wisdom is urged never to lose sight of sound thinking and careful discernment. Holding on to these truths brings vitality to a person's inner life and serves as a beautiful ornament of character. They keep a person grounded, sensible, and spiritually alive.

Those guided by God's wisdom can walk through daily life without stumbling into moral pitfalls or constant danger. At night, they can lie down in peaceful rest without anxiety or fear keeping them awake. Knowing that the Lord protects them gives quiet peace to their minds and bodies.

Believers need not panic when sudden troubles arrive or when storms of ruin strike the wicked. God Himself stands as their security and stronghold, keeping their feet out of hidden traps. Trusting in the Lord frees a person from terror even in dark and uncertain times.

When someone has the ability to help a neighbor or pay a debt, they should do it right away without making excuses. Putting off help until tomorrow when the money or assistance is available today is selfish and wrong. A truly godly person is eager to show love and meet the needs of others promptly.

It is wrong to plot harm against a neighbor who lives beside you in peaceful trust. It is also wrong to pick quarrels or drag people into lawsuits when they have done nothing to hurt you. God expects His followers to live peaceably and never betray the confidence of those around them.

We should never envy violent or crooked people, even when they seem powerful and successful in the world. The Lord detests those who use deceit and cruelty, and their success will not last. Instead, God shares close friendship and communion with those who walk uprightly.

The Lord places a curse upon the household and future of wicked people, no matter how grand their home may be. At the same time, God pours His blessing on the dwelling of the righteous, even if it is only a humble cottage. Real blessing does not depend on the size of a house, but on whether God is welcomed there.

God sets Himself against proud scoffers who mock at holy things, letting their own scorn bring about their downfall. To the humble, however, He freely gives His favor and undeserved kindness. Both Peter and James in the New Testament quote this verse to teach that God gives grace to those who lowly submit to Him.

Those who choose God's wisdom will receive lasting honor and a glorious heavenly inheritance. In contrast, foolish people who reject God will end up exposed to public shame and disgrace. A person's final standing before God and the world depends entirely on whether they lived by wisdom or folly.
